Context
-------
Read .github/copilot-instructions.md first. Then APPEND the following
rules to it — they are permanent repo conventions:

  - learner-vm provisioning scripts are ARTIFACTS. There is no AI on
    the airgapped network. The agent never executes them against the
    VM; the human operator does. Execution evidence for those arrives
    ONLY via feedback/airgap-run-*.md hand transcriptions. Never claim
    a provisioning script "works on the VM" — claim it "validates and
    self-diagnoses".
  - scripts/dev/* are the EXCEPTION: they run on THIS machine (online)
    and their outputs are committed artifacts the airgap VM consumes.
  - Every learner-vm provisioning script sources scripts/lib.sh, sets
    SCRIPT_NAME and SCRIPT_VERSION before sourcing it, is idempotent,
    and ends with the REPORT BEGIN/END block: <=60 lines, no ANSI
    colour, failures as F<n> with fix-hint + auto-run diagnostics,
    OK steps as a count, SKIPPED with reasons, and a NEXT line naming
    the next action.
  - step_fail ALWAYS runs its attached diagnostic commands and
    includes capped output (<=15 lines each) in the report.
  - On every edit to a learner-vm script, bump SCRIPT_VERSION and add
    a one-line comment above it describing the change.
  - Before touching learner-vm code, read feedback/airgap-run-*.md
    (newest first) and the current SCRIPT_VERSION comments.

Environment model (fixed facts)
-------------------------------
- The five workshop repos are public on GitLab; docs are public at
  https://o11y-workshops.gitlab.io/workshop-<track>/ for track in
  {opentelemetry, otel-developers, prometheus, fluentbit, perses}
- The labs have NO compose files. Every lab is a sequence of docker or
  podman CLI commands embedded in HTML. Labs exist in three path
  variants: labNN.html (docker), labNN-podman.html (podman),
  labNN-rancher.html (Rancher Desktop; same docker commands plus
  Rancher install steps).
- The lab VM runtime is PODMAN (rootful) behind the podman-docker
  shim — `docker` IS podman there. Both engines' commands land in the
  SAME rootful image store, so BOTH paths can be prebuilt.
- There is no docker-ce, no daemon.json, and no /etc/docker anywhere
  in this design.
- Recon counts: builds ~= fluentbit 21, opentelemetry 7,
  otel-developers 7, prometheus 4, perses 0.
- Known external images (8):
    docker.io/library/busybox:1.36
    docker.io/opensearchproject/opensearch-dashboards:3.3.0
    docker.io/opensearchproject/opensearch:3.3.1
    ghcr.io/fluent/fluent-bit:5.1.1
    docker.io/jaegertracing/all-in-one:1.76.0
    docker.io/persesdev/perses:v0.54.0
    docker.io/prom/prometheus:v3.13.1
    quay.io/prometheus/node-exporter:v1.12.1

Objective
---------
Produce and commit the content artifacts the airgap VM consumes:

  scripts/dev/import-content.sh   content acquisition (repos + docs)
  scripts/dev/parse-labs.py       -> content/extracted/*
  scripts/dev/patch-docs.py       -> rewrites content/docs/**.html
  scripts/dev/curate.py           -> content/extracted/curated.json

Committed outputs:
  content/repos/<track>/            five working trees, no .git dirs
  content/repos/<track>/.source-sha
  content/docs/<track>/             mirrored docs
  content/extracted/commands.json
  content/extracted/external-images.txt
  content/extracted/build-failures-expected.txt
  content/extracted/syntax-risk.txt
  content/extracted/parse-warnings.txt
  content/extracted/curated.json
  content/extracted/docs-patched.txt
  content/bin/docker-compose-v2 + content/bin/docker-compose-v2.sha256
  versions.lock                     (appended: repo SHAs, compose
                                     source URL + version, docs
                                     mirror date)

NOTE: prompt 10r's 00-diagnose script checks these outputs for
presence and integrity — the sha256 file matters.

import-content.sh
-----------------
For each of the five tracks:
  - source repo: reuse an existing clone if bundle/repos/<track> or
    content/repos/<track> already exists and is non-empty — copy the
    working tree WITHOUT .git into content/repos/<track>/; otherwise
    full clone of
    https://gitlab.com/o11y-workshops/workshop-<track>.git
    into a temp dir, then copy the tree without .git
  - write the HEAD SHA to content/repos/<track>/.source-sha and
    record it in versions.lock
  - docs: reuse bundle/site/<track> if present and non-empty; else
    wget --mirror --convert-links --page-requisites --no-parent
    https://o11y-workshops.gitlab.io/workshop-<track>/ into
    content/docs/<track>/; record the mirror date in versions.lock;
    verify a landing page exists
Idempotent: skip a track whose content/repos/<track> is non-empty and
has .source-sha, unless --refresh is passed.
Print a table: track | source SHA | lab*.html count | docs landing OK.

parse-labs.py
-------------
Walk content/repos/<track>/lab*.html — ALL variants, including
-podman and -rancher files. For each lab file record path_type:
    docker | podman | rancher     (derived from the filename)

For every container CLI command found in code blocks, record:
  type:         build|pull|run|network|volume|other
                (inferred from the first subcommand; `docker compose`
                or `podman-compose` usage flags type "compose")
  engine:       docker|podman   (the binary the lab invokes)
  sudo:         true|false     (whether the command was sudo-prefixed)
  raw:          the exact command text from the page
  tag:          -t value if build
  image:        image ref if pull/run
  context:      build context, resolved relative to the track repo
                root
  dockerfile:   -f value if present
  ports:        ["host:container", ...] from -p/-P
  name:         --name value if present
  detached:     true|false (-d)
  syntax_flags: [] or ["heredoc"|"buildkit-syntax"|"run-mount", ...]

Dockerfile syntax scan: for every build whose Dockerfile is readable
on disk, or whose Dockerfile content is embedded in the HTML, detect:
  - heredoc usage (<<EOF, <<'EOF', <<-EOF)
  - "# syntax=" BuildKit directives
  - RUN --mount= usage
Every build with any flag is ALSO written to syntax-risk.txt with the
lab filename. Rationale: buildah on RHEL 8.6 may not support these;
flagged builds must be SKIPPED (not failed) at preload time.

Base images: for every build whose context EXISTS on disk, read its
Dockerfile and extract every FROM line. For builds whose context does
NOT exist on disk (the attendee creates files interactively during
the lab), mark interactive_context=true and best-effort extract FROM
references from Dockerfile content embedded in the HTML.

Outputs:
  commands.json        full structure, lab order preserved:
                       { "<track>": { "labs": [ { "file",
                         "path_type", "commands": [ ... ] } ] } }
  external-images.txt  the 8 known external images PLUS every FROM
                       base image found across ALL paths, one per
                       line, as ORIGINAL references
                       (docker.io/..., ghcr.io/..., quay.io/...),
                       deduplicated and sorted
  build-failures-expected.txt
                       every build with interactive_context=true or a
                       missing context — EXPECTED to be skipped at
                       preload time, not failures
  syntax-risk.txt      flagged builds, with lab filenames
  parse-warnings.txt   anything ambiguous

Also print a per-track summary: labs parsed, commands by type, by
engine, and by path_type; the sudo split per path_type; base images
found.

patch-docs.py
-------------
Rewrite content/docs/<track>/**.html (a committed transformation —
git history preserves the originals):
  - banner div inserted after <body>:
      "OFFLINE LAB VM — all images are preloaded. Skip docker pull
       steps (marked PRELOADED). Supported paths: docker and podman —
       both use the same image store on this VM. For Rancher Desktop
       labs, follow the docker commands and skip the Rancher install
       steps."
  - rewrite `docker pull ...` AND `podman pull ...` inside code
    blocks to append "# PRELOADED — skip offline"
Log per-track patched-page counts to docs-patched.txt. Best-effort:
a page that fails to patch is a warning, not fatal.

curate.py
---------
From commands.json, derive per track the minimal tier-1 "this
workshop is alive" run set — the DOCKER-path (labNN.html, not -podman
or -rancher) commands that start the main services. Read the lab HTML
and the mirrored docs to choose; do NOT invent flags — copy the exact
flags from the lab commands. Each entry:
  { "name", "engine": "docker", "image", "ports": [...],
    "env": {...}, "volumes": [...], "cmd": [...],
    "check": { "url": "http://localhost:<port>/...",
               "expect": "<substring>" } }
Expectations to CONFIRM against the docs (the docs win on
contradiction — note it):
  fluentbit:       fluent-bit HTTP metrics port :2020
  opentelemetry:   Jaeger UI :16686 contains "Jaeger"
  otel-developers: Jaeger UI :16686 contains "Jaeger"
  prometheus:      :9090/-/ready contains "Prometheus"
  perses:          :3000 contains "Perses"; node-exporter :9100
                   metrics contain "node_"

docker-compose vendored binary
------------------------------
Download the docker-compose v2 static linux x86_64 binary (latest
stable v2.x release) and commit:
  content/bin/docker-compose-v2
  content/bin/docker-compose-v2.sha256
Record the source URL and version in versions.lock. Compose is NOT
load-bearing (zero usage in any lab) — robustness only. A later
provisioning script installs it against podman.socket.

Validation (all online — everything here really executes)
---------------------------------------------------------
- python3 -m py_compile on all three .py files
- run import-content.sh and paste the track/SHA/count table
- run parse-labs.py and paste the per-track summary
- paste external-images.txt in full
- paste build-failures-expected.txt in full
- paste syntax-risk.txt in full
- paste curated.json in full
- paste git diff --stat for the docs patch

Acceptance
----------
1. Command counts cross-check against recon: builds ~= fluentbit 21,
   opentelemetry 7, otel-developers 7, prometheus 4, perses 0 —
   report any divergence and which path it came from.
2. external-images.txt reviewed — a FROM image not in the known list
   is expected and fine; it just gets added. Flag genuine surprises.
3. curated.json reviewed — this drives both run-workshop.sh and the
   offline verification, so wrong entries here are expensive later.
4. docs-patched counts per track.
5. Explicit statement: everything in this prompt ran online; no
   learner-vm provisioning script exists yet or was touched.
